title: Enterprise Onboarding: Integrated Oncall, Escalation, Integration & QBR Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This playbook provides a single-source reference for the enterprise onboarding lifecycle at Redwood Inference: onboarding milestones, integration checklist, operational runbook for oncall and escalations, known issues and workarounds, and QBR / health-check guidance. Target audience: customer success managers (CSMs), solutions engineers (SEs), support engineers, SREs, and customer oncall responders.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-value for enterprise customers (target 4-6 weeks for first production call).
- Provide deterministic escalation paths and SLAs during onboarding and month 0-3 operations.
- Ensure consistent QBR content and measurable health checks for renewal conversations.

1) Onboarding phases and owner matrix

Phases (high level):
1. Kickoff (owner: CSM)
2. Integration & networking (owner: SE)
3. Validation & performance tuning (owner: Solutions/SRE)
4. Cutover & production launch (owner: CSM + SRE)
5. Post-launch monitoring & QBR cadence (owner: CSM)

Owner matrix (who does what):
| Phase | Primary owner | Secondary owner | Duration target | Deliverables |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Kickoff | CSM | SE | 1 week | Project plan, contacts, access matrix |
| Integration & networking | SE | Infra Eng | 1-2 weeks | VPC peering, routing, API keys, firewall rules |
| Validation & perf tuning | SRE | Eng | 1-2 weeks | Load test results, latency profile, batching config |
| Cutover & launch | CSM | SRE | 1 week | Production key rotation, runbook handed off |
| Post-launch & QBR | CSM | Product | Ongoing | Health metrics, QBR deck, action items |

2) Integration checklist (SE playbook)

Pre-integration checks (do these before any network work):
- Confirm contract terms: dedicated vs hosted, data residency, SLA tier.
- Obtain account IDs, org/team contacts, and primary technical POC.
- Verify required credentials and KMS/HSM access if Private deployment.

Network & security configuration steps:
1. Provide networking requirements doc to customer (CIDR ranges, ports 443/80, egress rules for telemetry endpoints).
2. For VPC/Private: validate VPN or Direct Connect, confirm NAT and route tables.
3. For Dedicated: confirm IP allowlist and service account creation.
4. Validate TLS and certificate pinning policy; rotate certs per security schedule.

API & auth validation:
- Exchange API keys; validate with a non-prod test key.
- Test token scopes for embeddings vs generation endpoints.
- Validate rate limit behaviour using the SDK quickstart.

3) Oncall and escalation runbook (support engineers + SRE)

SLOs and thresholds to trigger escalation:
- API error rate > 5% sustained for 5 minutes -> Page SRE (P1 if customer impact).
- 95th percentile latency > target latency * 1.5 for 10 minutes -> Page SRE + notify CSM.
- Queue depth / backlog > 4x expected -> Investigate routing and batching; page infra lead.

Escalation matrix (summary):
1. Support Tier 1 (CS/Support Engineer) - triage, customer comms, gather logs, basic remediation.
2. Support Tier 2 (SE / Support Engineer with infra access) - deeper debugging, replay requests, config checks.
3. SRE / Runtime Eng - kernel/runtime performance, capacity, autoscaling.
4. Product / Model Onboarding - model-specific regressions or safety incidents.
5. Executive escalation - only when SLA breach or major outage for >4 hours.

Paging procedure (numbered):
1. Identify incident and classify severity against the incident severity table below.
2. Collect essential context: customer org id, route/model, API key, timestamps, request IDs, sample request/response.
3. Attach traces and span ids from tracing system; include token-level latency if available.
4. Page the appropriate oncall role via PagerDuty with subject: [CS-INC] {customer} {sev} {short-desc}.
5. Notify CSM + account owner within 15 minutes for P1/P2 incidents.

Incident severity quick-reference:
| Severity | Customer impact | Target response | Example |
|---|---|---:|---|
| P1 | Production down / high error rate | 15 min | Entire API returns 500s for customer routes |
| P2 | Degraded performance / partial impact | 30 min | High tail latency for a subset of customers |
| P3 | Functional bug / single route | 4 hours | Single feature returns malformed output |

4) Known issues and workarounds (maintenance reference)

Top known items during onboarding (as of last_updated above):
- Issue: Intermittent 429s during initial load tests for Dedicated pools.
  Workaround: Temporarily raise client-side backoff to 2000ms and request a scheduled burst window with capacity team.
- Issue: Tokenization mismatch for specialized input encodings causing length miscount.
  Workaround: Pre-tokenize client inputs using the provided tokenizer CLI; enforce max_tokens= model_limit - 64.
- Issue: Private deployment TLS handshake failures with older OpenSSL versions.
  Workaround: Upgrade OpenSSL to >=1.1.1k or apply the compatibility patch in the onprem-packaging repo.

Known-issues table (short):
| Issue id | Symptom | Affected customers | Mitigation | Owner |
| KI-2026-001 | 429s under burst | Dedicated customers | Backoff + scheduled burst | capacity-planning@redwood.com |
| KI-2026-002 | Token length miscount | customers using custom tokenizers | Use provided tokenizer CLI | eng-serving-runtime |

5) Health checks and QBR material (CSM playbook)

Standard health metrics to collect (monthly):
- Availability (per-route, per-region) - target >= 99.9% for Dedicated customers.
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) - target < 0.5% sustained.
- Latency (P50/P95/P99) by route and model - compare to baseline at onboarding.
- Cost per 1k tokens and request mix (short vs long sequences).
- Model quality regressions: % of eval prompts failing acceptance criteria.

QBR agenda template (30-45 minutes):
1. Welcome & agenda (5m)
2. Usage & adoption trends (5-10m)
3. Reliability & incident review (5-10m)
4. Performance & cost optimization suggestions (5-10m)
5. Roadmap asks and action items (5-10m)

QBR deliverables:
- One-slide summary of health and top 3 risks.
- Action item tracker with owners and due dates (track in JIRA).
- Suggested optimizations: batching, quantization profile change, route pinning.

6) Cutover checklist (production launch)

Pre-cutover (24-72 hours):
- Confirm monitoring dashboards and alerting are in place and tested.
- Validate API keys and limits for production key.
- Run synthetic traffic at 1.25x expected peak for 30 minutes.
- Confirm rollback plan and traffic-shift schedule.

Cutover steps (ordered):
1. Migrate traffic using weighted routing (10% increments over 1 hour).
2. Monitor error rate and latency for each increment for 10 minutes.
3. If any P1/P2 thresholds breached, abort and execute rollback.
4. After full cutover, rotate keys and close migration ticket.

7) Post-launch 0-90 day playbook

Week 0-2: Stability focus - daily health check by SRE; CSM check-ins twice weekly.
Week 3-8: Optimization focus - run cost/perf tune, implement caching/batching suggestions, evaluate model recommendation from Redwood Optimize.
Week 9-12: Transition to standard support cadence - weekly then monthly QBRs, handoff to account success for renewals.

Appendices
A. Contact matrix and PagerDuty escalation roles (copy into account docs).
B. Example CLI commands for testing API:
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer {test_key}" -d '{"input":"Hello"}'
C. Troubleshooting checklist (quick):
- Confirm API key & route are correct.
- Fetch request trace ID and attach to ticket.
- Verify model version pinned during onboarding.
